title: Google Stock (GOOGL) Falls 2.2% as AI Stocks Slide (Nov 5)
summary: Alphabet (GOOGL) fell 2.20% to $282.57 on Nov 5, 2026, less than the Nasdaq's 5.52% drop, as AI stocks sold off after the midterm elections.
body_markdown:
## Why Google Stock Fell


The reports reviewed for this article named no Alphabet-specific cause for Thursday's decline. According to[Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/markets/stocks-nov-5-2026) , stocks plunged as the Democrats' midterm sweep fueled concerns about AI regulation and data center development, and the Nasdaq closed in correction territory, at least 10% below its October 6 record closing high. The outlet reported only that Google parent Alphabet also declined, one day after stocks rallied following the midterm elections.


Fox Business reported that rising electricity prices had turned the construction of power-hungry data centers into a political issue, with some Democrats calling for restrictions or pauses on new projects. eToro market analyst Jakub Rochlitz said markets are pricing in the midterm results.


> "The market's interpretation is that the AI infrastructure buildout will become slower and more expensive."
>
>
> Jakub Rochlitz, eToro market analyst, via Fox Business


As reported by[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/qualcomm-earnings-chip-stocks-election.html) , Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft, hyperscalers with infrastructure spending plans that extend well past $100 billion a year, each dropped between 2% and 4% on Thursday. CNBC noted that 41 local ballot measures in 10 states that would restrict data center construction went to a vote on Tuesday, November 3, according to Ballotpedia, and that Meta President Dina Powell McCormick said on Wednesday night that building data centers is "going to be harder" following the elections. Per CNBC, a[disappointing earnings forecast from Qualcomm](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/chip-earnings-selloff-qualcomm-arm-marvell/) also contributed to the selloff.


## GOOGL Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- According to[Alphabet's third-quarter 2026 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm) , consolidated revenue increased 25% to $127.6 billion, and CEO Sundar Pichai said the company is "now on a half-trillion dollar revenue run rate."
- Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.7 billion from $15.2 billion a year earlier, and Google Search & other revenue grew to $63.4 billion from $56.6 billion, per the same[earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) .
- GOOGL's 2.20% decline was smaller than the losses in Meta, Microsoft and Nvidia during Thursday's selloff.


### Risks


- Alphabet's purchases of property and equipment rose to $51.4 billion in the third quarter from $24.0 billion a year earlier, and free cash flow for the quarter was negative $9.1 billion, according to the company's release.
- Restrictions on data center construction were on local ballots in 10 states, and Meta's president said building data centers is "going to be harder" after the elections, as reported by CNBC.
